12 A box is shown resting on the ground. Newton’s third law implies that four forces of equal
magnitude are involved. These forces are labelled P, Q, R and S.
Forces P and Q act on the box. Forces R and S act on the Earth.
For clarity, the forces are shown slightly separated.
P
box
ground
Q
R
S
Which statement about the forces is correct?
A
P is the equal and opposite force to Q and both are forces of contact.
B
Q is the equal and opposite force to P and both are gravitational forces.
C
R is the equal and opposite force to S and both are forces of contact.
D
S is the equal and opposite force to Q and both are gravitational forces.

hints: Notice from the stem that P and Q both act on the box while R and S both act on the Earth, so any third law pair must take one force from P or Q and one from R or S.
Recall that a Newton third law pair must be the same type of interaction, so separate the upward contact push P from the downward gravitational pull Q on the box.
Compare the downward arrow Q on the box with the upward arrow S on the Earth and check whether both describe Earth-box gravitational attraction.
walkthrough: Identify the four forces from the diagram and stem: P is up on the box, Q is down on the box, while R is down on the Earth and S is up on the Earth.

State the Newton third law rule: the paired forces act on different bodies, are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction, and are the same type of force such as both contact or both gravitational.
Sort by type: P is the normal contact force of ground on box, so its pair must be the contact force of box on ground, which is downward R on the Earth.
Similarly, Q is the gravitational force of Earth on box, weight acting down, so its pair must be the gravitational force of box on Earth, which is upward S on the Earth.
Therefore P pairs with R as contact forces and Q pairs with S as gravitational forces. P with Q cannot pair because both act on the same body.
This matches the statement that S is the equal and opposite force to Q and both are gravitational forces. This is option D

A.explanation: P and Q both act on the box, so they cannot be a Newton third law pair. Also Q is a gravitational pull, not a contact force.

B.explanation: P and Q both act on the box, so they cannot be a Newton third law pair. Also P is the upward contact normal force, not a gravitational force.

C.explanation: R is a downward contact force of the box on the ground but S is an upward gravitational pull of the box on the Earth, so they are different types and cannot pair.

D.explanation: Q is the Earth pulling down on the box and S is the box pulling up on the Earth, so they are an equal and opposite gravitational third law pair.
